## Historical audit: S0069

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_probes/C1/selection/commons_138420790/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 of 3 is visible. The reference and render images themselves are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Line 16, student `model_request`, characters [0,173023) | The stated goal was an editable, single-image kitchen reconstruction, including geometry, viewpoint and materials. The student’s code inventories multiple objects: architecture, two timber posts, cabinetry, ovens, island, sink, hob, extractor and kettle. These are source-level objects, not independent confirmation that all are visible or correctly shaped. |
| Line 16, same event | A source-audit instruction requested checks for dimensions, keys, world initialization, hierarchy and material isolation. The student’s subsequent program added validation helpers and copied materials before extractor-subtree bump edits. This is evidence of receipt and implementation of that instruction; no separate teacher diagnosis is identified. |
| Line 16, step 1 and 2 results and student revision | Both reported `ok: true` and saved renders. After step 1, the student reported an undersized kitchen, central post and obstructing shell, hypothesized a camera outside the shell, and changed camera, wall and post. These are student observations and hypotheses, not independently verified pixels or causal proof. |
| Line 18, student `model_response`, [0,13685); line 19, `execute`, [0,14370) | The student reported step 2 cropping of the island, post and extractor, hypothesized excessive camera proximity, and supplied a third build. It moved the camera and post, raised the ceiling, lengthened the extractor and added suspension rods. The execute event contains that revision. |
| Line 20, `execution_result`, [0,59290); line 21, `select`, [0,59) | Step 3 reported success, finished a 16-sample render, and saved an image and blend file; step 3 was selected. This is **formal execution success**, not verified visual or geometric correctness. |
| Line 17, student `codex_session`, [0,3909) | The fresh read-only session had zero tool calls; images were supplied in the request. The visible exploration was iterative production rendering and student comparison, not diagnostic probing. |

**Scene checks and uncertainty.** The source defines different colors, wood-grain strips and a procedural extractor bump; their rendered appearance is unknown. Named child parts and suspension rods show intended grouping and connections, but contacts and composite movement were not independently tested. Camera pose and framing were explicitly revised; lighting was retained across the later revisions. The logs show rendering, but not whether lighting, occlusion or framing matched the photograph. In particular, the student’s camera-distance and extractor-height explanations remain hypotheses.

**Transferable lesson:** separate a reported discrepancy from its proposed cause, and preserve object ownership and local material isolation during revisions. **Task-specific choices:** the kitchen inventory, camera coordinates and extractor supports. Final visual fidelity, actual support contacts, any subsequent review, and results in unseen chunks remain unknown; no algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption is established here.
